# Every control in the back-office

**Generated by `scripts/design-audit/collect.mjs` — do not edit by hand.**
Parsed with the TypeScript compiler, not pattern-matched, so the counts are exact.

**416 controls**, of which **247 are buttons**.

| Control | Count | Styled | Dynamic class | No class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `button` | 247 | 123 | 10 | **114** |
| `input[text]` | 51 | 9 | 0 | **42** |
| `select` | 27 | 0 | 0 | **27** |
| `role=dialog` | 17 | 17 | 0 | **0** |
| `input[checkbox]` | 13 | 0 | 0 | **13** |
| `input[radio]` | 11 | 0 | 0 | **11** |
| `textarea` | 9 | 0 | 1 | **8** |
| `input[number]` | 8 | 0 | 0 | **8** |
| `input[time]` | 8 | 0 | 0 | **8** |
| `input[color]` | 8 | 0 | 0 | **8** |

| `input[password]` | 2 | 0 | 0 | **2** |
| `input[date]` | 2 | 0 | 0 | **2** |
| `input[url]` | 2 | 0 | 0 | **2** |

A control with no class renders as the browser default — which is how a destructive
action ends up looking identical to a safe one.
